About the Model
100,000 simulated seasons per run from an ensemble of rating systems and market prices, with home-field advantage, every conference's official tiebreakers and the 12-team playoff bracket. Ratings are on a points scale: the gap between two teams is the expected margin on a neutral field. 1,146 Kalshi markets priced. Δwk compares with the Sep 22 run. Model version 0.28.82.

Heisman projections53 candidates2% left for a winner outside the listStats and Kalshi prices Sep 29, 8:34 PM CT
Guide
# the Win % order - the table opens sorted by it
Player / Team his position beside his name; beside his team its rank in the Power Ratings (the PWR chip, 1 = the best team in FBS) and its record so far; click a team for its card
Proj Rec his team's projected regular-season record: expected wins - expected losses, to one decimal
QBR / EPA how efficient his season has been so far. A quarterback's Total QBR: a 0-100 grade of every play he makes - passing, running, sacks and fumbles - adjusted for the defenses faced (50 = average, 90+ = elite; Heisman-winning quarterbacks finished around 90). A back's or receiver's EPA per play: the expected points his plays added, not adjusted for the defense - receivers run higher than backs (a catch, not a carry), so each is colored against his own position. Hover for his percentile among FBS players of his position
Proj TD / Yds touchdowns and yards he is projected to be responsible for over the full season, title game included - passing, rushing and receiving together (the split on hover)
Base Score his Heisman Score in the base case - his average projected season - 0-100 with 50 = the average candidate here (most winners scored 98+ - Past Winners). It is graded against this week's candidates, so a Score moves when the others play, bye week or not. Win % can differ: it counts how often he finishes first across all simulated seasons, with the Kalshi price. Tap a player for what goes into it
Win % his projected chance to win the Heisman when ballots close (after the conference title games), with its American odds: our projection - the rest of the season simulated, and how Heisman voters have picked winners in the past - together with the Kalshi price. Part of the chance is left for a winner outside this list (the line above the table). One forecast among others, never a sure edge
Finalist his chance of being one of the four finalists invited to New York, with its American odds
Kalshi what a taker pays to buy YES right now - the ask plus Kalshi's fee - in cents (hover for bid / ask and the NO side)
Edge / eROI the better side for a taker now at his Win %, after fees: YES +4.9¢ = a YES bought now is worth 4.9¢ more than it costs; none = neither side pays. eROI = that edge over the price paid, shaded green from 25% (grey when neither side pays)
More columns adds his position, his team's record as a column of its own, its power rating (points better than an average FBS team on a neutral field), efficiency (passer rating for a quarterback, yards per touch for the rest), his team's projected losses and those against unranked teams, and American odds beside the Kalshi price. Show current stats adds the same stats so far, and the Score and win chance if the season ended today
Colors the stats are shaded against past Heisman finalists and winners when ballots closed: no color at an ordinary candidate's level, green from a lower finalist's level to full at a typical winner's (QBR against past quarterbacks; touchdowns, yards and efficiency against his position; team power, projected record and the rating; losses the other way), red below the average candidate; an unbeaten record shades green as the season goes on. The chances - Win %, Finalist and Curr % - are a different kind of number and shade violet instead (a violet line under their headers): a faint band down the column, darker the likelier (Win % full at 25%, the finalist chance from 20% to full at 75%). eROI shades green from 25%. Hover a column header for what it means
Tip click a player's row for his card - each stat now → projected at ballot time, bars for what he has banked of his projected touchdowns and yards, his Score and his chances (a small part of a total - a receiver's few carries - counts but is not listed); click a team for its card; click any column header to sort by it (again to reverse)
Base Score = his average (base-case) season · Win % = how often he finishes first across all simulated seasons, with the Kalshi price
